title: Building a Self-Hosted Runner Environment knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Building a Self-Hosted Runner Environment?
options: Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
A self-hosted runner fleet needs controlled registration, an up-to-date machine image, required tooling, restricted network access, and health monitoring.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
questions.answer_key: A self-hosted runner fleet needs controlled registration, an up-to-date machine image, required tooling, restricted network access, and health monitoring.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of building a self-hosted runner environment: A self-hosted runner fleet needs controlled registration, an up-to-date machine image, required tooling, restricted network access, and health monitoring. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

Choose runner labels and access boundaries that match the workload. Self-hosted machines need patching, network segmentation, secret protection, and cleanup; keep untrusted contributions away from privileged persistent runners.

questions.explanation: Runner machine requirements: Choose runner labels and access boundaries that match the workload. questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to building a self-hosted runner environment?
options: Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: A self-hosted runner fleet needs controlled registration, an up-to-date machine image, required tooling, restricted network access, and health monitoring. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
